title: Environmental regulations, circular economy practices, and firm performance: Mediating evidence from Vietnamese SMEs
content:
by Thuan Minh Tu, Quan Hong Nguyen, Phuong Ngoc-Duy Nguyen, Ho Hai Phan

Although sustainable management literature extensively addresses the link between organizational performance and sustainable practices, evidence on the mechanisms through which environmental regulations translate into firm performance remains inconsistent. Findings on whether circular practices mediate this relationship are mixed, particularly within SMEs, where these mediating pathways remain largely untested. The circular economy has arisen as a solution to address sustainability concerns. This study examines the influence of environmental regulations and circular supply chain management on sustainable firm performance. It emphasizes the mediating role of circular economy practices and the moderating impacts of top management green commitment. Employing Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling on survey data from 482 Vietnamese SMEs, the results indicate that both environmental regulations and circular supply chain management positively influence business performance, with circular economy practices acting as a partial mediator. Moreover, top management green commitment moderates the relationships between environmental regulations and circular economy practices and between circular supply chain management and circular economy practices, showing that top management green commitment determines how effectively environmental regulations and supply chain practices lead to circular economy actions - a finding that adds new insight beyond the widely recognized direct effect of leadership on sustainability outcomes. The results have significant implications for researchers, government officials, and company executives by elucidating how SMEs should adhere to environmental regulations and leverage circular supply chain management to enhance circular economy practices for sustainable efficiency in the context of developing countries. By integrating Institutional Theory and the Natural Resource-Based View, this study clarifies the regulatory and supply-chain pathways through which circular economy practices emerge, and how these practices translate into sustainable firm performance under varying levels of top management green commitment.
